open_points.subject: OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES
open_points.question: What is this scalar constant's type, exact value and serialization: which Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Path, Domain, expiry/Max-Age and other Set-Cookie attributes does it contain, and in what order or representation?
options: A complete Set-Cookie attribute suffix string
A structured immutable value that owner_interface serializes
Only policy flags, with routing and lifetime attributes supplied elsewhere
open_points.default_guess: Use a scalar suffix representing Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and a narrowly scoped owner-interface Path, omit Domain, Expires and Max-Age so it remains a host-only browser-session cookie.

open_points.subject: session cookie request scope
open_points.text: the session cookie's name `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` and its attributes `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES`
open_points.question: How must the cookie attributes ensure that the owner-session cookie is not sent to the service API when the two configured listeners use the same host with different ports, given that browser cookies are not scoped by port?
options: Require disjoint URL paths and scope the cookie to the owner-interface path
Require different host names for the two listeners
Permit the browser to send the cookie to the service API and require that surface to ignore it
Interpret “Registry's own origin” as including both Registry listeners
open_points.default_guess: Require a dedicated owner-interface path prefix and set the cookie's Path to that prefix.

witness.initial: The owner interface listens on `127.0.0.1:8781`, the service API listens on `127.0.0.1:8782`, and the owner has signed in.
events: The owner interface sets the owner-session cookie using `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES`.
A browser makes a request to a service-API route on the same host.
outcomes: The cookie is sent because cookies are host/path scoped and the chosen Path also matches the service route.
The cookie is not sent because the design requires disjoint paths or hosts and the attributes scope it to the owner interface.
witness.observer: The browser, the service API, and anyone inspecting the request see the difference.

open_points.subject: A19 required test 5 non-text rendering
open_points.text: a value that is not text in the text it is shown as
open_points.question: What canonical text representation must the renderer use for each non-text stored type, including instants, dates, numbers, booleans, enum members and absent values?
options: Define owner-interface display formatting per type
Use the programming language's generic string conversion
open_points.default_guess: Use the models' canonical wire representations, with UTC ISO-8601 text for instants and dates, decimal text for numbers, enum wire values for enums, and render absent values as an empty field.

witness.initial: A stored record contains a UTC instant and an enumeration value that an owner page displays.
events: The renderer converts the non-text fields to text.
outcomes: The instant and enum use their canonical wire forms.
The instant is localized and the enum uses a human-facing label or generic language string.
witness.observer: The owner and the required test see different page text.

open_points.subject: A19 required test 5 URL-context coverage
open_points.text:
every stored value a page of the owner interface shows —
   a value that is not text in the text it is shown as — in each kind of
   place it shows one — an element's content, an attribute's
   value, a value of a link's query — shown as that text
open_points.question: Does the test require each stored value to be exercised in every listed HTML context, including a query parameter, or only require every context actually used by the product to be tested with a value that may legally appear there?
options: Test only real value-to-context placements; never put personal values or secrets in a URL for the test
Exercise every stored value in all three contexts, including query parameters
Exercise every non-secret value in all three contexts but exclude personal values
open_points.default_guess: Test the real placements only, using a non-personal value for the query context and never introducing a personal value or secret into a URL.

witness.initial: A project display name is stored as personal data and contains `?`, `#`, `%` and a space.
events: A test author implements the new A19-1 coverage.
The owner opens the generated page.
outcomes: The test places the display name in a link query to satisfy a Cartesian reading of “every stored value” and exposes personal data in the URL.
The test checks the display name only where the product displays it and uses a permitted identifier for the query-context case.
witness.observer: The owner, browser history, request logs and the test suite see the difference.
